language_shifts.shift: Baseline: shortest FLS topics list; qualifier word list contains 20 terms ending with 'may'; cautionary statement reads 'not guarantees of future performance and involve risks, uncertainties, and assumptions that we cannot predict'; uncertainty attribution framed as 'our actual results may differ materially from the future performance that we have expressed or forecast'

COVID-19 language shifts from 'recent outbreak of COVID-19' to 'COVID-19 pandemic'; 'strive' added to qualifier word list; basis statement expands from 'ourselves and our industry' to 'ourselves, our industry, and the global economy and financial markets generally' — first signal of broadened macroeconomic uncertainty acknowledgment

FLS topics grow to include two new forward-looking areas: (1) 'our anticipated level of cash distributions or contributions, such as our dividend rate and contributions to our qualified pension plans' — signals management re-committing to capital return during COVID downturn; (2) 'the expected timing applicable to such capital investments and any related projects' — first explicit timing specificity added to capex guidance

Most significant linguistic shift in the series: qualifier word list expands by 6 terms to 26 total ('strive, seek, potential, opportunity, aimed, considering, continue' added); cautionary statement materially escalates from 'risks, uncertainties, and assumptions that we cannot predict' to 'known and unknown risks and uncertainties, the ultimate outcomes of which we cannot predict with certainty'; new FLS topics added: Winter Storm Uri frequency expectations, government restrictions and vaccine language, share repurchase program reintroduction, low-carbon fuel standards, and 'several carbon transition projects, which are in early development'

Uncertainty framing widens further: 'expressed or forecast' becomes 'expressed, suggested, or forecast'; new FLS topics: hedge transactions, counterparty credit risk, deferred tax repatriation, debt securities transactions; GHG targets upgraded from vague 'carbon transition projects in early development' (Q4) to 'our publicly announced GHG emissions reduction/offset targets' — commitment now public and trackable

COVID risk disclosure adds 'requirements and mandates with respect to vaccines' and 'administrative costs' to the impact list; otherwise stable vs Q5 — linguistic equilibrium reached; the broader hedging framework from Q4 is normalized rather than further escalated

red_flags: Share repurchase program entirely absent from Q1-Q3 FLS topic lists; reintroduced in Q4 — suspension implied by topic omission but never explicitly disclosed as a commitment change in the available safe harbor sections

Carbon transition projects described in Q4 as 'several carbon transition projects, which are in early development' — structurally non-trackable commitment with no investment scale, timeline, or technology disclosed

Cautionary language escalation from Q3 to Q4 ('known and unknown risks... cannot predict with certainty') is material and coincides with Winter Storm Uri losses, suggesting internal recognition of elevated operational uncertainty

The provided MD&A text contains only boilerplate safe harbor sections (~8,000 characters per quarter); substantive OVERVIEW AND OUTLOOK and RESULTS OF OPERATIONS sections were not included in the data extract, limiting the ability to track specific financial guidance delivery against actuals

notable_shifts.observation: Baseline: 20-word qualifier list; cautionary statement says 'not guarantees of future performance and involve risks, uncertainties, and assumptions that we cannot predict'; uncertainty statement: 'our actual results may differ materially from the future performance that we have expressed or forecast'

COVID-19 framing escalates from 'recent outbreak' to 'pandemic'; qualifier list adds 'strive'; macroeconomic scope explicitly widened; otherwise structurally similar to Q1 — management absorbing COVID shock without yet expanding hedging vocabulary further

Two new forward-looking topics introduced: dividend/pension commitment and capital investment timing — both additive specificity signals. Corn-related co-products added to product scope. Underlying cautionary language unchanged from Q2

Largest single-quarter linguistic expansion: qualifier word list grows from 20 to 26 terms; cautionary language upgrades to 'known and unknown risks and uncertainties, the ultimate outcomes of which we cannot predict with certainty'; six new FLS topics added including Winter Storm Uri, vaccine distribution, share repurchase reinstatement, low-carbon standards, and early-stage carbon transition projects

Uncertainty framing broadens: 'expressed or forecast' becomes 'expressed, suggested, or forecast'; three new financial disclosure topics added (hedge transactions, deferred tax repatriation, counterparty risk); GHG targets shift from 'early development' to 'publicly announced' — accountability now explicit

Incremental additions only: COVID impact list gains 'requirements and mandates with respect to vaccines' and 'administrative costs'; language otherwise stable vs Q5. Pattern suggests the deterioration in communication confidence peaked at Q4-Q5 and has stabilized rather than continued to worsen
